audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side read Yasuo (agreeing with win[N] and the packet), but every phases[N].why underneath described LUX winning that stage — the row said one thing and the sentence under it said the opposite.
audit.why: This is the exact 189-row defect from previous champions: the why strings were the generic Lux template and were never re-pointed when the sides were set to the enemy.
audit.corrected: All seven whys rewritten from the Yasuo-wins verdict, grounded in Wind Wall's 25/23/21/19/17s cooldown and 4s duration, Sweeping Blade's 475 range, and Last Breath's 70/50/30s. Sides and win[N] already agree, so no chart-group edits were made.

audit.why: spikes[] has all four entries and the level 6 / first-item / late progression matches the kit: Last Breath needs a knockup, crit items outpace Lux's Luden's timing, and late Yasuo flanks behind Wind Wall.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single decisive interaction was stated only vaguely: Wind Wall blocks ALL enemy projectiles for 4 seconds, and every one of Lux's four spells — Q, W, E and R — carries the projectile flag. breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all, so the 25-to-17s wall cooldown and 70s Last Breath never reached the page. Sweeping Blade also cannot be re-cast on the same target for a few seconds, which is what makes the LAST hop of a dash chain the bindable one.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds' and 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds'. Both are the concrete sequencing this matchup runs on.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field now carries the real numbers; dosFull[1] rewritten around the re-cast restriction; tradeGood/tradeBad and enemyWin re-grounded.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim; dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0..1].d were generic templates that could be pasted onto any enemy.
audit.why: Lint findings COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2 plus the template sweep on the dos/donts bodies.
audit.corrected: Five bullet bodies rewritten inside the length band, each tied to its own title and to Yasuo's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The recorded win rate is 50.78% over 3572 games, but the page rates the lane HARD at 8/10 with a blanket Yasuo sweep of all seven rows.
audit.why: A near-even win rate does not square with the enemy owning every stage of the lane. I could not resolve which is right from the kit alone, so the rows were left where they stand.
audit.corrected: No change made; flagged for the user.

edits.before: E-poke from max range on his last-hits — the slow zone plus passive auto is your chip engine from level 1.
edits.after: Wind Wall is not up yet, but his passive shield builds while he moves and eats most of one E's chip damage.

edits.before: Q joins: the root threat re-prices every step he takes past the wave's midline.
edits.after: At 2 he has Sweeping Blade: 475 range, near-zero cooldown, and it closes on your 1175.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-E-auto with the passive detonations is a real chunk. Shield his answer and walk.
edits.after: Wind Wall is up: 4 seconds that eat Q, W, E and R alike. Every spell you own is a projectile.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact. Bank Manaflow and hold Q for his aggression, not yours.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks make a knockup, and his E resets through the wave feed them. Hold Q to peel.

edits.before: Final Spark online — anything the root catches dies to the laser math. The lane becomes a geometry quiz.
edits.after: Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 and needs only one knockup — his level 6 threatens more than your Final Spark.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-E-R deletes squishies from root range. Force him to dodge or die on every contact.
edits.after: His crit item outpaces Luden's here: he dashes in, walls the snare, and finishes before you cast twice.

edits.before: Late Lux decides fights from a screen away: root the entry, slow the pit, and laser the clump your team froze.
edits.after: He flanks from fog and a 17-second Wind Wall covers his whole approach — your team locks him or you die.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Check it before every step-up. - W Prismatic Barrier is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5, and 4 seconds of uptime that blocks Q, W, E and R alike — every spell you own is a projectile. - Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 and needs a knockup first. - Your Q is 10s: it is peel, not poke.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade cannot re-cast on the same minion right away — bind him when the dash chain runs out of bodies, not on the first hop.

edits.before: Yasuo whiffs Wind Wall and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks mean a knockup — shield before the second.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Q is 10s and a projectile — a held Sweeping Blade dodges it and Wind Wall deletes it.

edits.before: Your W answers exactly one combo per fight — shield the spell that kills, not the one that stings.
edits.after: His Q and E are both 475 range; inside that with your 10s Q down you have nothing that stops the knockup.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: His passive shield builds while he moves, so his approach costs him nothing; at 475 he is one Sweeping Blade from you before W lands.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: E the far side of the wave and detonate as he steps in — chip him while Wind Wall is on cooldown, and keep Q banked to peel the dash.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Throwing Q at a moving Yasuo with Wind Wall up — he blocks it, dashes in, and your only peel is on a 10-second timer.

edits.before: Good trade: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning. Bad trade: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Good trade: E the far side of the wave and detonate as he steps in — chip him while Wind Wall is on cooldown, and keep Q banked to peel the dash. Bad trade: throwing Q at a moving Yasuo with Wind Wall up — he blocks it, dashes in, and your only peel is on a 10-second timer.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by raising Wind Wall over your Q, dash-stacking Steel Tempest through the wave, and knocking you into Last Breath.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by making him spend Wind Wall on a cheap E, then binding the dash chain's last hop and lasering him before the shield rebuilds.

notes: The whole full-layer level chart pointed at Yasuo while every why described Lux winning; all seven whys were re-pointed. Sides and win[N] already agreed, so no chart-group edits were needed. Wind Wall's exact re-cast restriction duration on Sweeping Blade ('a few seconds') is not numeric in Riot's text, so it is stated qualitatively. breakdown.wave, ahead, breakdown.early/mid/late and breakdown.feeding still read as templated Lux boilerplate; a grounded replacement did not fit the ±10% band without dropping real content, so they were left alone.
